title: Innocent post on dev'ing from the pub 🍻 still turned to an anti-AI extravaganza 🤷🏻‍♂️🤦🏻‍♂️
author: logical_haze

comments.author: MatsutakeShinji
comments.body: Vibe coding while relaxing is a pleasure ngl.

comments.author: iliark
comments.body: I don't get people who can dev on just a laptop. A laptop as a portable machine to bring to and from work where you connect to a large monitor, full keyboard, and separate mouse, sure. But trying to do work on a tiny screen, sitting in a non-ergonomic chair at an unideal desk height with tons of distractions around you?

replies.author: logical_haze
replies.body:
That laptop connects at home to a bigger setup of course. But into my 12th hour of coding that day, I wanted a change of scenary. 

And it was mostly deploying stuff and waiting, not excessive coding

replies.author: gefahr
replies.body:
I have written some of the best code of my life with my laptop on my knees on my back in bed in the middle of the night.

When you're in the zone the rest really doesn't matter. *Getting* there on the other hand, yeah, the ergonomics are a big deal for me too.

replies.body: Oh boy, you'd be surprised, I actually prefer a laptop than a desktop, allows me so much more flexibility, I take it back and forth from work. I guess it's just a different mindset and getting used to it so much I don't feel right in front of a desktop computer at times.

comments.body:

replies.author: imnotabot303
replies.body: In the old days when I was at school my maths teacher would always try to get us to do as much as possible without a calculator. When someone complained he would say "When you're out in the world you're not always going to have a calculator in your pocket".

replies.author: Segaiai
replies.body: I don't know about advanced math, but you do need to build quick intuition about division and multiplication, compounding, and more to avoid countless real life issues, and the more math you can do in your head, the better off you'll be. Far less likely to fall for scams, make far better long-term decisions, etc... If you have to write it all out, it's probably not as useful, though to build that intuition, you generally do have to write it out at least at first.

replies.author: imnotabot303
replies.body: Yes I know, it was just a funny thing for him to say in hindsight. Relying on any tech to do the thinking for you is never a good thing. Education is obviously about teach you how to get the answer not the answer itself.
